notes: The handle plate with gauge tile and yellow slope (b46-b48) and the briefcase (b49) are minifigure accessories. The doctor carries them beside the car on page 15, and nothing fastens them to the car. The doctor minifigure is not in the 62-piece inventory, so it is not a node. To avoid leaving them as separate islands, I added `contact` (rest) edges from b46 and b49 to the vehicle base b1. This is an assumption: the manual shows no fastened connection, so these are loose, unfastened contacts only.

The pictures do not label every piece, so I assigned some pieces to steps from the part shapes. Examples: the 1x4 white brick b24 and plate b25, the 1x1 bricks b32/b33, the tiles b16/b20/b21/b37/b38, and which 1x2 tile goes in the rear assembly versus the lightbar.

Most stud/anti-stud joins use null ports because the stud grid position is not clear from the small isometric pictures. Ports are given only where the stacking order is clear (grille on the bumper brick, the step 10 stack, the roof, the lightbar, the accessory).
The steps are shown with the base upside down at first (steps 1-2). I put the black 2x3 plates and wheel holders on the base ends as shown there.
The doors b29/b30 are hinged to the base as an assumption. The pictures do not show the hinge points clearly, and the catalogue gives the doors only a single hinge port.
The two cupboards sit side by side across the rear body. Each has its own door slid in, and the roof side tiles b37/b38 sit one on each cupboard. The trans plate b34 spans both cupboards.
The catalogue's wheel holder has no pin port, so the wheel pin-hole joins to b4/b5 use a null port on the holder. Copies 1-2 go on b4 and copies 3-4 go on b5.
The sticker sheet is joined to the roof as a representative adhesive connection; the stickers also go on the cupboard doors (step 13).
